key_insight: Brain-Adapter uses a dual-stream MIL design to combine text-guided visual attention with global scan-level learning for more accurate 3D CT diagnosis of acute intracranial pathologies.
clinical_relevance: It could make brain CT interpretation more scalable in acute care by reducing dependence on dense manual annotations while supporting multi-label scan-level diagnosis.
method: Text-Conditioned Attention uses raw report sentences as semantic queries to focus on disease-relevant image regions.
A parallel visual MIL stream learns global scan characteristics from structured labels extracted by an LLM.
A consistency constraint and uncertainty-aware refinement module align and fuse the two prediction streams.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments showing Brain-Adapter outperforms state-of-the-art 3D models and standard MIL baselines on scan-level multi-label classification.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of report text, label extraction, and careful validation before deployment in real clinical workflows.
paper_title: Brain-Adapter: A Dual-Stream Vision-Language MIL Framework for Comprehensive 3D CT Diagnosis of Acute Intracranial Pathologies
